principles: Improve agent routing without changing gate authority.
Prefer exact next commands over prose-only guidance.
Keep scope_check_save reviewer-written, not main-agent self-signed.
Keep checklist_add advisory about milestone ledgers; do not infer or auto-create ledger rows.
drivers: The current failure wastes command budget before DEV.
The PLAN scope-check dispatch gap blocks this story before implementation can begin.
The checklist_add ledger-sync gap made milestone_status look misleading after CHK-006 was added.
The safety contract must not be weakened by convenience automation.

options.name: M0-M1 plus minimal #6 dispatch and checklist_add ledger hint
pros: Addresses the largest INIT discovery waste and the PLAN blocker that prevents this story from reaching DEV.
Keeps evidence contracts unchanged because scope_check_save remains reviewer evidence.
Prevents checklist_add from silently creating ledger/status drift while keeping milestone_status read-only.
Can be tested with focused command-output and dispatch assertions.
cons: Broadens the first slice beyond pure M0-M1.
Does not yet solve M2 checklist self-seeding, M3 parser/schema fixes, M5 asset repair, or M7 ceremony redesign.

options.name: M0-M1 plus minimal #6 only
pros: Smaller than the chosen scope and addresses the immediate PLAN scope reviewer blocker.
cons: Leaves checklist_add capable of hiding new checklist work from milestone_status until an agent manually notices ledger drift.
Would make future agents rediscover the same checklist/milestone mismatch.

options.name: M0-M1 only
pros: Smallest original slice and lowest blast radius.
cons: Leaves the current story blocked at PLAN by the documented #6 gap.
Leaves the checklist/milestone guidance bug unaddressed.

options.name: Implement all M0-M7 milestones at once
pros: Could reduce all known friction in one broad effort.
cons: Large blast radius across parser, dispatch, help, assets, tests, and ceremony policy.
Higher risk of accidentally weakening gate semantics.

options.name: Skip routing and add an express lane
pros: Could make trivial tasks faster on paper.
cons: Cross-vendor audit vetoed agent-self-attested risk/size downgrades as an evasion bypass.
Would attack ceremony cost before measuring discovery-cost fixes.

chosen: M0-M1 plus minimal #6 dispatch and checklist_add ledger hint
rationale: The user explicitly requested the checklist/milestone mismatch be solved in this same pass. The safest implementation is a command-output hint from checklist_add when a ledger exists: it fixes the rediscovery problem without letting checklist_add invent milestone claims or mutate gate evidence.

preMortem.scenario: A help or session hint says init_preflight is enough to advance
preMortem.trigger: Wording blurs read-only diagnostics with gate evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Agents overclaim readiness or skip required reviewer/scope evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Every new hint must keep init_preflight read-only and mention story_advance only after prerequisites are satisfied.

preMortem.scenario: Scope-plan dispatch becomes gate evidence by implication
preMortem.trigger: The new dispatch path returns a prompt and agents treat that as a pass.
preMortem.consequence: PLAN could advance without reviewer-written scope_check_save evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Prompt and tests must state dispatch output is not gate evidence; reviewer must call scope_check_save.

preMortem.trigger: The ledger-sync hint is implemented as automatic milestone mutation instead of guidance.
preMortem.consequence: Milestone claims become guessed from checklist prose and ProofStory intent accounting weakens.
preMortem.mitigation: Only print an advisory next command; do not mutate milestone-ledger.json from checklist_add.

preMortem.scenario: Tests assert brittle full help output
preMortem.trigger: Snapshotting too much global help text.
preMortem.consequence: Routine command catalog edits break unrelated tests.
preMortem.mitigation: Use focused substring/ordering assertions around init_preflight, scope-plan dispatch, and ledger-sync hint wording.

preMortem.trigger: While touching help/parser/dispatch files, nearby issues are tempting to fix opportunistically.
preMortem.consequence: Scope expands and review cannot isolate whether the routing fixes worked.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep M2 checklist self-seeding, M3 parser/schema fixes, M5 asset repair, and M7 redesign explicitly excluded.

preMortem.scenario: Fallback INIT attestation is misread as independent reviewer approval
preMortem.trigger: The story used init_check_repair fallback because subagent spawning was not explicitly authorized earlier.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers might overtrust the INIT gate evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve the fallback warning and rely on normal PLAN/DEV/REVIEW/TEST gates before any implementation claim.
